title: Make the task-completion hook commit by explicit owned pathspec
description:
Filed by governor-1a5aca5d 15:23Z under the human's standing sweep directive. The project's own global rail already declares this defect and its consequences ("The task-completion hook must commit by explicit pathspec... A whole-tree commit at completion is forbidden. Until the hook is fixed..."), but no task existed to fix it. This session produced 10+ occurrences.

THE DEFECT: at task completion, the wrapper/hook stages and commits the WHOLE TREE, sweeping every peer's in-flight untracked/modified files into a commit bearing the completing task's id.

MEASURED OCCURRENCES THIS SESSION (non-exhaustive): c970f10 (ff589) swept b785's deliverable + 7ba's step-5 test + 69's residue; 1576a44 (b785) same class; d447a34 (0c894) swept a cross-host probe; 11b78f2 (6cbff) swept b9378's benchmark WIP + the 88th boundary constant; e867ee9 (6f786, 26 files/1745 insertions) swept five of d4329's six paths mid-gate; 0237cfc (aa32fdf7) swept FOUR other slices' in-flight files; 1733d72 (d7b352e1) swept 16d5b's RED tests; c7013ad (3e54b466) swept c994bd0a's two security files AND was initially mistaken for a mislabeled/malicious commit (qa STOP alarm 14:53, later retracted) — the sweep class now generates false security alarms.

CONSEQUENCES BEYOND NOISE: (1) pathspec attribution is unauditable — the 13:33 producer-registers rule and any `git log -S`-based audit break silently; (2) QA must grade every task by base-ref diff instead of its commit; (3) workers must disclose "no commit bears this task id" on nearly every completion; (4) one sweep landed a half-written peer file into HEAD (the aa32fdf7 registry design mid-write).

THE FIX, per the rail's own words: the hook commits ONLY the completing task's declared owned paths (the task record carries affectedFiles/filesModified). Untracked peer files never enter the commit. Decide and pin: what happens when an owned path is missing or when non-owned changes are staged (fail closed with a stable code, never widen).

Verification: a test simulating a completion with a dirty peer file proves the commit contains ONLY owned paths and the peer file remains untracked/modified; a mutation restoring whole-tree staging turns it red.
definitionOfDone: The completion hook stages and commits by explicit pathspec derived from the completing task's owned paths; a peer's untracked or modified file is NEVER captured (test-proven with a dirty-peer fixture).
Missing owned path or unexpectedly staged foreign content fails closed with a stable reason code rather than committing a wider tree.
A mutation drill restoring whole-tree staging turns a NAMED test red.
The global rail's "until the hook is fixed" clauses are updated to reflect the fix, and the session's occurrence list above is cited in the completion note.
taskRails: Fail closed: never fall back to whole-tree staging on any error path.
Do not break the existing push-on-completion behavior; only the staging scope changes.
Re-measure the hook's current code path on current bytes before planning; the occurrence list is evidence, not a code map.

implementationPlan.description: STOP-AND-AUTHORIZE, plus premise correction. Read-only. NOTE ON THIS PLAN'S SHAPE: every step carries an EMPTY affectedFiles list, deliberately. The daemon validates affectedFiles against the moe-next project root and this task owns no file inside it; the real paths are absolute and named in each step's prose. That validation failure is itself evidence of finding (1). TWO findings must be settled before any edit. (1) RAIL CONFLICT: the hook does not live in this repo. `grep -rln "git commit\|git add" apps/ packages/ tools/ scripts/` inside D:/projexts/moe-next returns ZERO -- moe-next contains no staging or commit code at all, and `.claude/settings.local.json` has no hooks block. The hook is `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.ps1` and `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.sh`, outside the tree epic rail 2 pins development to ("Development happens only in D:/projexts/moe-next"). Obtain EXPLICIT human authorization for that rail exception, in writing in chat, and record the message id in the step note. If it is not granted, call `moe.report_blocked` naming those two absolute paths and the rail -- do not edit another repository on an inferred exception. (2) THE DESCRIPTION'S PREMISE IS PARTLY STALE, and re-measuring changes the fix. The hook ALREADY stages by explicit pathspec: ps1:2320-2325 and sh:2976-2978 loop `git add -- <path>` over the task's `filesModified`. Whole-tree `git add -A` is only the FALLBACK when `filesModified` is EMPTY (ps1:2332-2333, sh:2984-2986). The real sweep vectors are three and the description names only one: (a) that empty-list fallback; (b) the BARE `git commit -m "$MSG"` at sh:2997 and ps1:2338, which commits whatever sits in the SHARED INDEX regardless of what this hook staged -- precisely what epic rail 3 forbids agents from doing; (c) `filesModified` is known to include files the task only READ, so pathspec staging can itself stage a peer's modification to a file this task merely opened. Confirm all three on current bytes and write them into the step note before proceeding.

RED first, in the EXISTING post-flight harness `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/tests/postflight.sh` and its twin `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/tests/postflight.ps1` -- do not build a new harness. Add failing scenarios against a disposable throwaway git repo the test creates and destroys; never against a live project, because a post-flight test that commits into a real tree reproduces the very defect under test. Scenario A (dirty peer -- the DoD 1 case): task reports owned paths X and Y; peer file Z is modified and peer file W is untracked; run the post-flight commit path; assert `git show --stat HEAD` names EXACTLY X and Y, and that Z is still modified and W still untracked afterwards. Scenario B (pre-staged foreign index -- the newly measured dominant vector): task reports X; a peer has ALREADY staged Z into the shared index before the hook runs; assert the commit contains ONLY X and that Z remains staged and uncommitted. Scenario C (empty filesModified): assert the run refuses with a stable reason code and commits NOTHING -- assert the literal code string and that `git rev-parse HEAD` is unchanged, not merely that the command failed. Scenario D (a declared owned path missing from disk): same fail-closed behaviour under its own DISTINCT stable code, because "nothing to stage" and "a declared path does not exist" are different causes and collapsing them makes a later guard change invisible. Assert the scenario COUNT so a harness that silently generated zero scenarios cannot pass.

GREEN the bash hook, `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.sh`. Replace the bare `git commit -m "$COMMIT_MSG"` at ~:2997 with an explicit-pathspec commit over exactly the task's owned paths -- `git commit -m "$MSG" -- "$PATH1" "$PATH2" ...` -- so a peer's pre-staged index entry can never ride along. Delete the `git add -A` fallback at ~:2984-2986 and replace it with a fail-closed refusal carrying a stable reason code: an empty `filesModified` now means DO NOT COMMIT, loudly, never commit more. Keep the existing per-path `add` miss-tolerance, but COUNT the paths that actually staged and refuse with the distinct Scenario D code when that surviving set is empty. Record in a comment the hazard behind that counting rule: a pathspec naming an UNTRACKED file commits nothing for that path, so a success check on `git commit` exit status alone can report a commit that silently omitted a deliverable. Change nothing about push behaviour, the quality gate, or the REVIEW transition -- task rail 2 scopes this to staging and commit only.

GREEN the PowerShell twin, `D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.ps1`, making exactly the same three changes at ps1:2320-2338: explicit-pathspec commit, no `-A` fallback, fail-closed stable codes spelled IDENTICALLY to the bash side so an operator grepping either transcript finds the same string. The twins drift easily, so after editing, compare the two behaviours case by case against the step-2 scenario list rather than reading the code side by side. Windows specifics that must not be lost: quote every path (spaces are routine in these trees); do not let `$LASTEXITCODE` from a prior `git` call leak into the new commit's success test; and do not let `2>$null | Out-Null` suppression mask a genuine commit failure -- capture the exit code separately, exactly as the bash side already does deliberately at sh:2993-3001, whose comment explains that piping commit into `tail` would make the test read tail's status and turn a failed commit into a reported success.

Run the step-2 scenarios against both twins until green, then run the mutation drills that prove each guard is load-bearing. Drill 1: restore the bare `git commit -m "$MSG"` by dropping the `-- <paths>`; Scenario B must go RED. If only Scenario A reddens, the test is proving staging rather than commit scope and must be strengthened by actually pre-staging a peer file. Drill 2: restore the `git add -A` fallback; Scenario C must go RED. Drill 3: make the missing-path branch fall through to a commit instead of refusing; Scenario D must go RED. For each drill record the command, the failing scenario NAME, and the exact assertion that failed -- a drill that reddens by crashing, or on a different assertion, has not proven the guard. Restore exact bytes by re-editing after each drill (never `git checkout`) and confirm with `git -C D:/projexts/moes diff --numstat -- scripts/` showing 0 added and 0 deleted. Run one drill at a time.

Handle the distributed copies and the rail text -- both implied by the DoD, neither named in the description. (a) COPIES: `D:/projexts/moes/moe-vscode/bundled/scripts/moe-agent.sh` and the moe-jetbrains sandbox copy under `moe-jetbrains/.intellijPlatform/sandbox/...` also carry this code. Determine by measurement whether each is a build artifact regenerated from `scripts/` or a hand-maintained fork. Regenerate the artifacts through their existing build step; if any is a fork, say so explicitly in the completion note and do NOT hand-patch a sandbox directory. A fixed source with stale shipped copies is a half-fix and must be disclosed as one. (b) RAIL TEXT: DoD 4 requires the global rail's "until the hook is fixed" clauses to be updated -- its two standing consequences for WORKERS and QA stop being true once the commit is pathspec-scoped. Draft the replacement text but do NOT edit the rail unilaterally: propose it via `moe.propose_rail` or route it to the governor, and record the proposal in the completion note. A rail is board state, not a file this task owns.

Adversarial self-review, then commit. Read the diff as an attacker: can ANY path still reach a whole-tree stage or a bare commit -- including an error branch, a `set -e` bypass, or a PowerShell `-ErrorAction` swallow? Does an owned path containing a space, a glob character, or a leading dash reach `git` correctly, or does `--` placement let it be parsed as an option? Since `filesModified` is known to include files the task only READ, can the new code commit a peer's modification to a file this task merely opened -- and if so, is that acceptable, or must the path set be filtered to actually-modified paths? Decide, and state the decision in the note rather than leaving it implicit. Does the refusal path leave the worker loop in the same state the old fallback did, so a fail-closed commit does not silently strand a finished task? Are the bash and PowerShell reason codes spelled identically? Then commit: this task's edits live in D:/projexts/moes, so run `git -C D:/projexts/moes status --porcelain`, unstage any foreign entry, and commit ONLY the four owned script paths by explicit pathspec -- practising the exact discipline being shipped -- then verify with `git -C D:/projexts/moes show --stat`. Cite the session's occurrence list from the description (c970f10, 1576a44, d447a34, 11b78f2, e867ee9, 0237cfc, 1733d72, c7013ad) in the completion note as DoD 4 requires.

Verification gate. Read-only. Run in the FOREGROUND, chained with `&&` so a red leg cannot be masked -- a `;` chain reports only the last command and a pipe reports the tail's exit code, which is exactly the bug the bash hook's own comment at sh:2993 warns about. From D:/projexts/moes run `bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh && pwsh -File scripts/tests/postflight.ps1`. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: confirm each of the four scenarios A-D is NAMED in the output with a result, and that the printed scenario count equals four -- a harness that silently ran zero scenarios exits 0. Because this task's edits are outside moe-next, ALSO run `pnpm typecheck && pnpm test` from D:/projexts/moe-next and confirm this task left the moe-next tree untouched (`git status --porcelain` there must show no entry owned by this task), so the rail-2 exception is demonstrably contained to the two script files. This command's fresh output is the sole `complete_task` verification evidence.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected: (a) planning this against moe-next -- measured, moe-next contains no staging or commit code whatsoever, so there is nothing here to fix and a plan pretending otherwise would be fiction; (b) editing D:/projexts/moes without asking -- epic rail 2 pins development to moe-next and an architect may not grant itself an exception, so step 1 makes explicit human authorization a precondition and report_blocked the alternative; (c) taking the description's fix at face value ("the hook commits ONLY the completing task's declared owned paths") -- re-measurement shows the STAGING is already pathspec-scoped and the actual leak is the BARE COMMIT over the shared index plus the empty-filesModified fallback, so implementing the description literally would change nothing about the dominant vector; (d) keeping a whole-tree fallback behind a louder warning -- the DoD and the task rail both require fail-closed, and every measured occurrence happened while that warning was already printing. Note on plan shape: affectedFiles is empty on every step because the daemon validates those paths against the moe-next project root and this task owns no file inside it; the real absolute paths are named in each step's prose.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Measured 2026-08-17 on current bytes. moe-next: `grep -rln "git commit|git add" apps/ packages/ tools/ scripts/` returns nothing; `.claude/settings.local.json` has keys [permissions, enabledMcpjsonServers] and NO hooks block. The hook lives in D:/projexts/moes/scripts/moe-agent.ps1 and moe-agent.sh, which are near-twins. BASH: reads `.moe/tasks/task-<id>.json` via a small node one-liner and pulls `filesModified` (sh:2962-2972); if non-empty it loops `git -C "$PROJECT" add -- "$TASK_PATH"` per path with miss tolerance (:2976-2978) and reports leftover dirty paths (:2979-2982); if EMPTY it prints a yellow warning and runs `git add -A` (:2984-2986); then, if `! git diff --cached --quiet`, it runs a BARE `git commit -m "$COMMIT_MSG"` (:2997), capturing the exit code separately because -- per its own comment -- piping commit into tail would report tail's status. POWERSHELL: identical shape at ps1:2320-2325 (per-path add), :2332-2333 (the -A fallback), :2335-2338 (bare commit). So staging is ALREADY scoped and the SHARED INDEX is the leak: epic rail 3 already states that a bare `git commit` captures another task's staged files, and the hook is doing exactly what that rail forbids agents from doing. A third vector the description never names: `filesModified` is known to include files the task only READ, so pathspec staging can stage a peer's modification to a file this task merely opened. A post-flight test harness ALREADY EXISTS at scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1 -- that is the test home, not a new harness. Distributed copies exist at moe-vscode/bundled/scripts/moe-agent.sh and under moe-jetbrains/.intellijPlatform/sandbox/; classify each as artifact or fork by measurement rather than patching blindly.
planningNotes.risks: The load-bearing risk is fixing the wrong vector: a change that only scopes STAGING lands green and changes nothing, because staging was already scoped and the bare commit is what sweeps the index. Scenario B (peer file pre-staged before the hook runs) is the only test that distinguishes them, and drill 1 exists to prove it does. Second, a fail-closed change that strands finished work: once the empty-filesModified fallback refuses, a task that legitimately reports no files must still leave the worker loop in a sane state -- decide that behaviour rather than discovering it in production. Third, a pathspec naming an UNTRACKED file commits nothing for that path, so a naive success check on `git commit` exit status can report a commit that omitted a deliverable; count what actually staged. Fourth, paths with spaces, globs or leading dashes need correct quoting and `--` placement in BOTH shells. Fifth, the twins drift -- verify behaviour case by case against one scenario list rather than reading the two files side by side. Sixth, run every scenario against a disposable throwaway repository. Seventh, shipped copies under moe-vscode and moe-jetbrains can leave the fix half-landed; classify and disclose. Finally, the rail-text update in DoD 4 is board state: propose it, never edit it unilaterally.
